vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: my-stock
Version: 1.0.0

The 'my-stock' skill bundle is a stock market analysis tool providing real-time quotes, limit-up tracking, and portfolio management. The analyzed files (SKILL.md, README.md, and utility scripts) show no signs of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injection. The scripts (check_api.py and test_skill.py) are standard health-check and testing utilities that interact with a local backend server, and the documentation is consistent with the stated financial analysis purpose.

llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and resource needs are consistent with a local-stock-analysis assistant and do not request unrelated credentials or unusual installs.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (stock quotes, limit-up, shareholder dynamics, portfolio) align with the provided files and instructions. The SKILL.md, README, and scripts all describe a FastAPI backend + optional frontend and use of pywencai for data; these are reasonable requirements for the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions direct the agent to interact with a local backend (http://localhost:8000) and to run/inspect the backend; that matches the skill purpose. Minor inconsistency: scripts/test_skill.py queries an endpoint /api/search-stock that is not listed in the SKILL.md API table (SKILL.md lists /api/stocks etc.). Otherwise instructions do not ask for unrelated files, system-wide credentials, or external endpoints beyond described data sources.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec in the registry (instruction-only), and the repository files provide standard Python scripts. No downloads from arbitrary URLs or unusual installers are present in the provided files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables. README and SKILL.md mention optional AI_PROVIDER/AI_API_KEY and a .env.example for optional AI integration — this is proportionate for an AI chat feature but the variables are optional. No unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill does not request permanent presence (always: false) and does not modify other skills or system-wide settings. It expects to run a local service and access local JSON files for caching, which is consistent with a self-hosted backend.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent: it expects you to run a local FastAPI backend and optionally provide AI API keys if you use the AI chat feature. Before installing or running: 1) Only run code from this skill if you trust the source — the package includes a backend server (inspect backend/main.py and ai_service.py). 2) The skill will make HTTP calls to http://localhost:8000; ensure you run the included backend or understand where the data comes from. 3) Optional AI_API_KEY may be needed for the AI assistant — if you don't intend to use the AI feature, you can leave it blank. 4) Small mismatch: test script calls /api/search-stock which isn't listed in SKILL.md — review the backend's endpoints to confirm behavior. 5) If you plan to run it, run the provided scripts in a sandbox or VM first, and review requirements.txt and any third-party dependencies (pywencai may require additional configuration or credentials).
